title: follower F5: binary wiring + Limitations
description: main.rs: PeerClient, Hub::with_peers/with_local_key_material, Fanout::spawn with Follower, router(directory, hub, follower); docs in lib.rs/main.rs. Smoke test: binary config with two peers. See .7 design field (approved plan) and decisions mimid-1wgh.7.2..mimid-1wgh.7.17.
notes:
From F2: (a) record follower_member when a relayed update is accepted (F-Q6) — F2 left it to the caller since the store code is F3's; wire it here. (b) Relay is a standalone struct (Relay::new(Arc<Hub>, PeerClient)); hold it inside Follower. Relay and hub keep separate directory caches (fine; note).
From F3 (adcd1bd): router already takes follower (done early, approved). Remaining: give Follower its PeerClient (binary currently refuses every /notify 403); a store fn for adding follower_member outside Welcome matching (needed for (a) relayed updates and room creation); leave() not implemented — scope it to what F-Q6 needs, file a bead for anything beyond; subscribe() unfiltered by design. From F4: call Follower::with_key_packages and Hub::with_local_key_material in main (HTTP keyMaterial for our user in a remote room answers 501 until then); update the two lib.rs Limitations bullets that say so. Own messages stay echo-only (F-Q5 reaffirmed 2026-10-18).
Approved by Mark 2026-10-18: join point = seq snapshot before the relay request; leave() local-only and idempotent (the agent's leave flow sends the real removal); set_relay after construction; room-creation membership recorded by the .12.4 caller; hub<->follower Arc cycle for process life (documented). Left for F6: own-domain fanout->follower e2e, hub-proxied keyMaterial and relay over real HTTP, relay_update membership vs a real hub.
